page.layout: One printed page. Top: a four-line epigram in roman type above a rule, full width. Below the rule: a marginal note in the left margin ("Consiliarius Badensis &c."), a centred title head, then the body of verse in italic with a large initial P. A catchword-like word "Sancta" sits at the lower right, beside the last lines. Faint show-through of another page is in the right margin and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Quem quis diligit, hunc monet: monendo Hunc & vulnerat: at periculosa Ejus basia sunt: atroce qui te Infestans odio deosculatur.
main_text.head: VVALTHERVS RETICHIVS: Tu vir charus Helvetiis.
main_text.p: Consiliarius Badensis &c.PRaeclarißime Vir, Retichiorum Gentis gloria, Principisque dulce Tui delicium: quod a Latinis Trito fertur adagio Poëtis, Fatis nomina congruunt frequenter: Pulchrè juppiter id tibi applicarim. Nam quòd HELVETIIS suâvis atq; CHARUS VIR sies: hic vel unus actus Clarè comprobat, auspicante jovâ, Tuo Principe sic jubente, fedus Tam laudabile, forte, Christianum Quod tu dexteritate singulari, Fide, judicio, eloquentiaque, Felix sollicitâris, impetrâris, Fedus Principe Marchione dignum: Binâ & principe Civitate dignum: jure hinc surgit honor tibi perennis: jure hinc surgit amor tibi perennis. Macte hoc, macte animo! juvare Christi Gloriam, patriæ bonumque perge. Vides Imperium ut labascit: ejus Robur ut quatitur rebellione:

page.notes: The epigram and the body are set in roman and italic; the printed hyphen-less line ends are kept as printed. "Sancta" at lower right is a catchword-like word, kept in the bottom_margin. Show-through from the reverse page appears faintly in the right margin and is omitted. Some letters in the verse are uncertain (e.g. "Helvetiis" and the swash capitals) and were read from the scan.
